trust_decision.summary: Whether a per-file disk write stream (and its fd) is released, and the storage callback settled, when the client aborts mid-upload; decided in disk storage's _handleFile/_removeFile, with per-file write accounting in the middleware.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'file descriptor leak on aborted uploads'. The only fd producer is fs.createWriteStream plus file.stream.pipe(outStream), and pipe never closes the destination when the source is destroyed.

fix_sites.entry_point: multer.diskStorage()._removeFile, called from the middleware abort cleanup at lib/make-middleware.js:146-148

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/make-middleware.js:237-242 and lib/make-middleware.js:300-316 (pendingWrites accounting in the middleware that wraps the storage engine; fix.diff:13-23, fix.diff:31-46)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The pendingWrites counter is correct at the pinned commit and the report is about disk fds. It becomes a double decrement only once disk storage also reports the source error through cb (pipeline), so a solver who fixes only storage/disk.js sees nothing wrong in the middleware. That fix lets the abort cleanup run early while another file's write is still in flight, which leaves an orphan file.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Completed files must still report size/path from bytesWritten and be unlinked immediately by _removeFile. Files cut off by the fileSize limit (`aborting`) must still be recorded for removal. Other in-flight files must finish before cleanup. An over-broad fix (destroying or waiting on every stream in _removeFile, rejecting on any destroyed state, or adding a cb(err) path without idempotent accounting) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: source stream already destroyed before the write stream opens (storage/disk.js:38; fix.diff:86-87)
source destroyed mid-write after createWriteStream (storage/disk.js:44-46; fix.diff:95-100)
abort cleanup unlinking a file whose write stream is still open (storage/disk.js:58-66; fix.diff:109-128)
multi-file request where one file's error is reported twice, via the stream 'error' event and the storage cb (lib/make-middleware.js:237-242, lib/make-middleware.js:306-310; fix.diff:13-38)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Memory storage pipes file.stream into concat-stream and settles cb only on finish, so an aborted upload never settles the storage callback (no fd involved, only buffered chunks).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Memory storage holds no file descriptor, and the abort path skips the pending-write wait (lib/make-middleware.js:180), so the advisory's fd/DoS property arguably does not apply.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, sibling file of the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second disk engine, e.g. write-to-temp-then-rename or a hashing engine, that copies the pipe/finish pattern
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: StorageEngine.md:50-69 documents exactly the leaky pipe/finish/unlink pattern as the template for custom engines, so a maintainer-written second engine would copy it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another early-abort path (e.g. a per-file timeout or mimetype sniff limit) that sets `aborting` and decrements pendingWrites directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fileSize limit path already uses this shape; a new limit would naturally follow it and reintroduce the non-idempotent decrement.

O9_family: resource release on error path (CWE-459 incomplete cleanup / CWE-400 fd exhaustion)

O10_build.project_tests: test/orphan-file-cleanup.js, test/async-file-filter-orphan.js, test/error-handling.js:453 (client abort), test/disk-storage.js. The fix's own fd tests read /proc/self/fd and are skipped off Linux.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap pipe for pipeline (or destroy outStream on source error) in storage/disk.js only, leaving the guard at storage/disk.js:38 returning silently, _removeFile unlinking before close, and the middleware counter decrementing twice.

out_of_scope_notes: StorageEngine.md:50-69 documents the same leaky pipe/unlink pattern for third-party engines (documentation, not code).
